A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, figures, equations, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original five-fold NER experiments on SEPR PHI and MEDDOCAN, alongside diversity and privacy measurements, including Appendix B results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original NER, diversity, and privacy experiments, including the appendix results, with several revised table entries.

M1.justification: The QLoRA domain adaptation, GPT-SW3/FLOR synthesis, encoder-based annotation, and synthetic NER training pipeline remain unchanged. Appendix A's model-name correction and training-restart disclosure do not establish a newly introduced method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Swedish SEPR PHI and Spanish MEDDOCAN for clinical PII detection. No dataset, language, domain, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain the same comparators, including gold-trained NER models and synthesis without domain adaptation. Revised gold-baseline scores do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported training grid from five fractions, including 10%, to four: 5%, 25%, 50%, and 95%. Table 1 already contained these four fractions in v1, making this a limited protocol-description correction rather than evidence of rerunning experiments.

E4.justification: The ablations of domain-adaptation data, annotation data, generator size, and synthetic-corpus size are retained. Diversity and privacy analyses, including Appendix B's 3-gram and 10-gram results, are unchanged; the new diagram illustrates an existing analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix A newly discloses conditional training reruns when an encoder predicts only the zero class. This adds information about unsuccessful-run handling, without specifying restart counts or establishing increased independent repetitions. Five-fold mean and standard-deviation reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 4's MEDDOCAN gold score changes from 0.973±0.004 to 0.978±0.005. Table 5 revises gold scores from 0.920±0.008 to 0.926±0.005 for SEPR PHI and from 0.977±0.005 to 0.978±0.005 for MEDDOCAN; its MEDDOCAN 400% synthetic entry changes from 0.973±0.004 to 0.973±0.003. Other results, including Appendix B, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 1's n-gram recall definition and its restriction to PII-overlapping n-grams are unchanged. Figure 2 visualizes the existing sets R, R*, and S without adding mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions retain the same claims: modest domain-adaptation data and smaller generators can suffice, while machine-annotator quality largely determines downstream utility. The conclusion preserves their scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of utility, memorization, and cross-institutional applicability remain stable, as do limitations concerning task generalization and n-gram privacy proxies. The paragraph explaining that synthetic data are no privacy panacea moves from Section 8 to Section 5.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly explains that MEDDOCAN's original splits were merged before five-fold resampling. Appendix A discloses restarting collapsed encoder training with unchanged data and hyperparameters, and corrects the encoder name from FLOR to roberta-base-bne. These clarify existing experiments; hyperparameter values, software versions, and computational estimates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds HHS (1996) to support a footnote distinguishing HIPAA-defined PHI from broader PII. The substantive related-work positioning is retained; other bibliography edits update metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, adds short explanations, and relocates one privacy paragraph into the discussion. The section sequence and overall narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the n-gram-set diagram in Figure 2, replaces the placeholder captions for Tables 8 and 9 with descriptive captions, and refines other captions. Tables are repositioned as text flows differently, while Figure 1 and the overall two-column design are retained.

improvement.justification: The revised baseline entries in Tables 4–5 and corrected training-fraction list improve internal consistency. Split and restart disclosures, completed appendix captions, and the explanatory diagram improve reproducibility and clarity. These resolve localized reporting defects while leaving the study's evidence and substantive limitations largely unchanged.
